data.description: Reaction-wheel torque and momentum capacity carry a margin of at least 30 % against sustained worst-case disturbance torque
Throughout the mission, the attitude control subsystem maintains the pointing performance required for observation operations and the safety of the vehicle, including under anomalies
The attitude determination error in steady-state observation mode is at most 0.01 deg (3σ)
The observation-mode control law achieves a pointing control error of at most 0.05 deg (3σ) in the presence of attitude determination error 0.01 deg (3σ) and disturbance torques
Starting from the maximum tip-off rate 10 deg/s, B-dot control damps the body rate to a safe-mode-transition level within 2 orbits
From both post-separation and FDIR re-entry conditions, the satellite completes detumbling and reaches safe mode without external intervention
The disturbance torque model (gravity gradient, aerodynamic, solar radiation pressure, residual magnetic moment) envelopes the disturbances actually acting in the target orbit (500-600 km altitude)
The detection conditions and transition sequence for attitude anomalies (rate exceedance, loss of attitude determination, wheel failure) guarantee safe-mode arrival within 10 min of detection
The inertia tensor and mass properties used for control design deviate from the real vehicle within the control system's stability margins
Throughout the mission, accumulated reaction-wheel momentum never reaches saturation, and interruptions to observation operations stay within the planned unloading schedule
The magnetorquer dipole moment provides sufficient control torque for B-dot control across the geomagnetic field strengths of the target orbit (500-600 km altitude)
In steady-state observation mode, the pointing control error is at most 0.05 deg (3σ)
The rate information required for detumbling remains available under gyro failure, from redundant sensing including estimation with coarse sun sensors and magnetometers

In safe mode, the satellite maintains, without external intervention, a state satisfying all of the following:

- The angle between the solar-array normal and the sun direction stays within 30 deg (positive power balance)
- Mode transition completes within 10 min of anomaly detection
- All mission equipment is off and every unit stays within its thermal safety range
In the safe-mode configuration (all mission equipment off, sun angle within 30 deg), generated power exceeds the configuration's consumption under all orbit conditions including eclipse
Safe-mode sun pointing acquires the sun starting from the residual rates left after detumbling, and thereafter keeps the sun angle within 30 deg
Periodic magnetorquer unloading has an unloading capacity exceeding the disturbance momentum accumulation rate, and is compatible with the observation schedule
